surfaces.part: sign front board with 국밥 lettering

answer.evidence: Rows 1-3 are a light band (L~238) that widens from 12 to 15 px. Row 4 is a darker gray-blue line (L=132), which acts as the front-edge line. Row 5 is a dark outline/shadow row directly under it. Together they form a 4-row top surface. Below, rows 6-29 are the tall front board carrying the lettering, and row 30 is a gray base strip, giving about 25 rows of front face. The darker strip on the right (x~11, rows 6-29) reads as shading on the front face, not a receding side face. The top is a trapezoid, not an ellipse, but the edge line and shadow are enough evidence of a top surface.

surfaces.part: top cap band of sign frame
sign board face with Korean lettering

answer.evidence: The sign is a tall flat board. Rows 6-29 are a dark red face with cream lettering, and a darker strip on the right (x≈11+) is shading, not a receding side face. Rows 1-4 are a pale cap band with rounded corners (widths 10, 12, 14, 15). Row 30 is a gray-blue base band that matches the row 4 line, so the top reads as a mirrored frame cap, not a horizontal surface. It has no ellipse, no foreshortened depth and no contents. At most a 2-row rim is read as top, so this matches the 'front elevation: top 1-2' wrong references.
